Definition: accusative case of G1431 as adverb; gratuitously (literally or figuratively):--without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain.
BiblicalUsage: Freely, without a cause, the adverb of the free gift. Jesus told the disciples to give freely because they had received freely, and He was hated without a cause, exactly as the psalm said. Paul insists we are justified freely by God's grace, and warns that if righteousness came by the law, Christ died in vain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe freely is the only word that fits what God has done for me. I received without paying, so I give without charging, and I refuse any gospel that puts a price on what Christ gave His life to make free.
